# 22. Legal, Privacy & Compliance

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Ensure the static site has the right notices, consent behavior, claim controls, and legal review for its audience and data practices.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A jurisdiction and audience record covering where the business operates, where users are targeted, and whether children or regulated sectors are involved.
- [ ] A privacy policy that accurately describes data collected, purpose, legal basis where required, processors, retention, rights, contact, and updates.
- [ ] A cookie or tracking notice where non-essential cookies, local storage, pixels, embeds, or analytics require disclosure or consent.
- [ ] A terms, disclaimer, accessibility statement, refund policy, or professional notice where the business model requires it.
- [ ] A data processing inventory for forms, analytics, embeds, maps, video, fonts, CDNs, email marketing, and booking tools.
- [ ] A consent record strategy for marketing opt-in and tracking consent where required.
- [ ] A copyright and licensing register for fonts, icons, images, videos, code, copy, testimonials, and client logos.
- [ ] A legal review owner for regulated claims, privacy compliance, advertising disclosures, and industry-specific obligations.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Legal pages must match actual site behavior and third-party services.
- [ ] Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, and revocable where GDPR-style consent is required.
- [ ] Rejecting non-essential tracking must not break essential site access.
- [ ] Marketing consent must be separate from service inquiry submission where required.
- [ ] Disclosures must be clear, conspicuous, and near the relevant claim or action.
- [ ] The site must not imply legal, medical, financial, or professional guarantees without qualified review.
- [ ] All media and code must have rights suitable for public commercial use.
- [ ] Privacy and legal content must be updated when tools, forms, tracking, or jurisdictions change.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check all data collection points against the privacy policy.
- [ ] Check cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, pixels, external embeds, and analytics scripts before consent.
- [ ] Check that consent accept, reject, change, and withdrawal behavior works.
- [ ] Check that affiliate, sponsored, testimonial, guarantee, pricing, and results claims are disclosed where needed.
- [ ] Check that accessibility statements do not claim compliance not supported by audit evidence.
- [ ] Check that image, font, icon, and script licenses are stored or linked.
- [ ] Check that contact details for privacy requests are current.
- [ ] Check that legal pages are linked from footer and relevant forms.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid copying privacy policies from unrelated sites.
- [ ] Avoid pretending static sites collect no data when forms, analytics, logs, embeds, or CDNs process user data.
- [ ] Avoid dark-pattern consent banners, prechecked boxes, bundled consent, and hidden reject options where prohibited.
- [ ] Avoid unlicensed stock images, copied competitor copy, and logo use without permission.
- [ ] Avoid publishing legal advice unless the business is qualified and reviewed.
- [ ] Avoid treating this checklist as legal advice.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The privacy experience must be honest, readable, and aligned with the site implementation.
- [ ] Compliance must be designed into forms, tracking, embeds, and copy before launch.
- [ ] Legal risk must be reviewed by qualified counsel for the relevant business and jurisdictions.
- [ ] Every public claim must be supportable if challenged.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use audits to inventory tracking scripts, storage usage, forms, external embeds, missing privacy links, and license-sensitive assets.
- [ ] Use generated legal page templates only as placeholders requiring legal review.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Required pages cover privacy, terms/legal, cookie notice, accessibility statement where appropriate, sitemap, contact details, company info, disclaimers, funding notices, returns/refunds where selling, and footer links.
- [ ] Cookie and analytics UX provides clear banner/options, accept/reject/manage choices, remembered preferences, mobile/keyboard accessibility, policy alignment, and no optional analytics before consent where required.
- [ ] Industry rules cover healthcare, finance, legal, education, e-commerce, portfolio confidentiality, testimonials, before/after claims, pricing, guarantees, and responsible disclaimers.
- [ ] Privacy planning defines form data, analytics data, cookies, consent, third-party processors, embedded tools, sensitive data avoidance, user rights, and contact route.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
